key.label: Fit the Choc switches
key.note: Both pairs of keys are spaced equally. Fit each black socket before pressing the switch in from above. Fit the battery last, with the soldered wires flat against the backplate.

carrier.label: Key holder with rounded finger beams and integral battery spring

steps.title: Solder the Sockets Off the Holder
steps.caption: With the holder off the rod and upside down on the bench, solder each socket's two wires outside the holder. Keep solder on the terminal tabs, not above them.

steps.title: Slide In the Lower-Left Socket
steps.caption: Slide the wired socket in from the outside edge, slightly towards the hinge. Centre it below the two contacts, then lift it onto them.

steps.title: Slide In the Lower-Right Socket
steps.caption: Hold the socket about 2 mm below its seat and slide it in from the right edge, above the thin guard runners, wires trailing outward. Under its seat, lift it straight up so the two bosses enter the backplate.

steps.title: Push Up the Upper Sockets
steps.caption: Bring each socket up about 1 mm away from the rod position, so its inner solder joint passes beside the ring arm. 2 mm below the seat, move it in and press it up.

steps.title: Tape Every Socket
steps.caption: Lay one strip of polyimide tape across each socket and its wires onto the backplate, as on R16. Press the tape ends onto the backplate with a flat tool. Keep pressure off the guard runners. The tape insulates the solder from the rod and holds the socket. On the left side keep the wires of both sockets flat against the backplate: the battery slides in under them.

steps.title: Press In the Switches
steps.caption: Back each socket from below with a finger or flat tool, then press each switch in from above until it clicks into the plate.

steps.title: Slide in the battery
steps.caption: Slide the disconnected pack in from the battery end. Leave about 4.5 mm beyond the back of the key holder. Keep the leads free.

dfr.label: OP1 and DFRobot paddle

housing.label: Fixed white housing under the OP1 board

plug.label: White plug on the wand harness

op1_wire.label: OP1 lead from the white plug

sensor.label: DFR0030 touch board, flat face up

connector.label: White Gravity socket under the board

sensor_lead.label: Three wires exiting beside the hinge

carrier.label: Key holder with rounded finger beams and integral battery spring

cap.label: Paddle with one long contact bar

post_bar.label: Two-post bar with wider board seats and narrow clip necks

lid.label: OP1 board retainer with lift stop (longer tower stems)

op1_lead.label: OP1 lead while the plug is threaded

steps.title: Thread the white plug up from below
steps.caption: Leave the black switch and the retainer off and unplug the white plug from the board. Tip the plug so its lead hangs straight down. Raise it beside the rod, inside the right finger guard, and up through the small opening at the end of the board seat.

steps.title: Turn the plug upright above the holder
steps.caption: Hold the plug above the holder with its socket face up. The lead runs back down through the opening.

steps.title: Push the board onto the plug
steps.caption: Hold the bare board level, white housing down, and push the housing onto the plug.

steps.title: Lower the board into its three holes
steps.caption: Lower the board straight down. Its three metal sockets drop into the three holes in the holder while the housing and plug sink into the opening and the lead slides down through it.

steps.title: Press the lead into its channel
steps.caption: From underneath, press the lead up into the open channel beside the rod so it runs towards the hinge end.

steps.title: Fit the mouse switch
steps.caption: Line the three switch pins up with the OP1 sockets and seat the case squarely.

steps.title: Insert the two-post bar
steps.caption: With the paddle off the holder, line up both posts underneath it. Push the bar up squarely until the spring tips pass through and the bar seats.

steps.title: Connect the Gravity lead
steps.caption: Plug the three-wire lead into the white socket on the underside while the touch board is still loose.

steps.title: Seat the touch board
steps.caption: With the flat gold face up and the white connector underneath, lower the board over both posts. Guide the wires straight out between the hinge arms.

steps.title: Slide on the two small clips
steps.caption: Seat the touch board on the paddle. Lay each flat clip on the board and slide its open end around the narrow part of the post, under the head.

steps.title: Move the paddle over the holder
steps.caption: Line the barrel up between the two hinge cheeks. The sleeve faces the mouse switch.

steps.title: Lower the paddle
steps.caption: Lower it so the sleeve surrounds the switch and the barrel sits between the cheeks.

steps.title: Slide in the hinge pin
steps.caption: Lower the paddle onto both seats. Slide the pin through the three holes.

steps.title: Press in the pin clip
steps.caption: Slide one small clip in from behind until it grips the middle groove of the pin. Keep the second clip as a spare.

steps.title: Fit the OP1 retainer
steps.caption: Hold the paddle down. Slide the retainer in from the front, along both rails and over the OP1 board, until the latch seats.

steps.title: Press the lower half of the pad
steps.caption: Press and release the centre and either lower corner. The switch should click and return freely.

annotations.step: Fit the mouse switch
annotations.title: Bought switch. Its three pins plug into the board sockets. It fits either way round.

annotations.step: Fit the OP1 retainer
annotations.title: The retainer covers the board and latches in the left rail. Its two low posts sit over the feet of the paddle's two legs and limit paddle lift.

annotations.step: Press in the pin clip
annotations.title: Slide the centre clip in from behind the hinge pin.

annotations.step: Thread the white plug up from below
annotations.title: One window for the white plug and its lead. Bring the plug up beside the rod sleeve, on the guard side; the guard arm now runs clear of this path.

annotations.step: Thread the white plug up from below
annotations.title: Tip the plug so the lead trails straight down behind it.

annotations.step: Lower the board into its three holes
annotations.title: Three metal sockets, three fixed holes. The board rests on the deck around them.

annotations.step: Press the lead into its channel
annotations.title: The lead runs in this open channel under the deck, clear of the rod.

dfr.note: Fit the OP1 board, switch and paddle in order. Run the three touchpad wires straight towards the top of the keypad, between the matching hinge arms and over the pin clip.

xiao.label: XIAO holder and keeper
xiao.note: Fit the R25 holder and keeper together to try the stronger catch. The board sits in its original position. Keep the USB-C socket, reset button and antenna end accessible. The keeper belongs to this XIAO holder, not the battery.

keeper.label: R25 keeper and rounded lift tab

steps.title: Lay In the Board
steps.caption: Tilt the near end of the board up about 6 degrees, slide the USB end under the two far fingers, then lower the near end onto its ledges. Side wires stay outside the walls. Underside solder must leave room: see the clearance map in geometry-checks.json.

steps.title: Point the Tooth Toward the Holder
steps.caption: Line up the two side ears with the grooves. The small tooth faces down and the rounded edge faces the board.

steps.title: Slide On the Keeper
steps.caption: Push along the grooves until the tab drops behind the ridge. The prongs rest over the two corners of the board.

steps.title: Pull Gently to Check the Stop
steps.caption: A small straight pull brings the tooth against the steep face. The board prongs stay flat.

steps.title: Lift the Rounded Tab
steps.caption: Lift the rounded edge a little with a fingernail. The tooth rises above the ridge.

steps.title: Slide the Keeper Out
steps.caption: Keep the tab raised while you slide the keeper back along its two grooves.

steps.title: Let the Tab Settle
steps.caption: Let go once the tooth is clear. The spring tab returns to its flat shape.

steps.title: Lift the Board Out
steps.caption: Lift the keeper end of the board and slide the USB end out from under the far fingers.

xiao_latch.label: XIAO keeper detail
xiao_latch.note: Side section of the matching R25 parts. The bend is drawn from the checked CAD route.

holder.label: Blue holder ridge and steep face

keeper.label: Orange keeper tooth and spring tab

steps.title: Find the Ramp and Tooth
steps.caption: The orange spring is joined to the keeper outside this side section. The blue ridge has a slope on the way in and a steep face on the way out.

steps.title: Push Until It Clicks
steps.caption: The tooth climbs the blue slope. The tab drops flat once the tooth passes the steep face.

steps.title: Pull Gently to Check the Stop
steps.caption: A small straight pull brings the tooth against the steep face. The board prongs stay flat.

steps.title: Lift the Rounded Tab
steps.caption: Lift the rounded edge a little with a fingernail. The tooth rises above the ridge.

steps.title: Slide the Keeper Out
steps.caption: Keep the tab raised while you slide the keeper back along its two grooves.

steps.title: Let the Tab Settle
steps.caption: Let go once the tooth is clear. The spring tab returns to its flat shape.

finger_rest.label: Click-end finger rest
finger_rest.note: The click is at the bottom. The guard on the right sits beside the battery.

carrier.label: Key holder with rounded finger beams and integral battery spring

steps.title: Index finger at the click end
steps.caption: The two long branches on each side follow the same rounded curves. Beside the battery, the guard is open at the outside edge so the black socket can slide in.

whole.label: Complete rod assembly
whole.note: The battery and both finger guards are carried by the keys on the 500 mm rod.

steps.title: Start with the bare rod
steps.caption: Keep one end clear to slide the holders on in order.

rodMounts.lastStep: Press the lower half of the pad
rodMounts.title: Slide the keys onto the rod
rodMounts.caption: Slide the assembled keys down the free end to the farthest position.

rodMounts.title: Slide the empty cable clip onto the rod
rodMounts.caption: Fit the empty clip between the battery and XIAO positions before feeding the wires.

rodMounts.lastStep: Pull Gently to Check the Stop
rodMounts.title: Slide the XIAO holder onto the rod
rodMounts.caption: Guide the rings onto the free end and slide the holder beside the cable clip.

whole.finalCaption: Check the battery holds in the rails, the pad clicks freely, and all wires clear the controls.
